definitions.gloss: to start doing; to begin; to set about
definitions.explanation: To begin an action or activity, often with a sense of suddenly or energetically getting started. More casual and vivid than {始|はじ}める.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもたちが{庭|にわ}でサッカーをやり{出|だ}した。
examples.english: The children started playing soccer in the yard.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{一度|いちど}やり{出|だ}すと{止|と}まらない{性格|せいかく}だ。
examples.english: He has the kind of personality where once he starts something, he can't stop.

notes:
A compound verb combining やる (to do) + {出|だ}す (auxiliary verb indicating the start of an action). The ～{出|だ}す pattern is productive in Japanese, attaching to many verbs to express the sudden or spontaneous beginning of an action.

More colloquial and energetic than {始|はじ}める. Often implies that the action began somewhat abruptly or without much deliberation.

COMMON PATTERNS:
The ～{出|だ}す auxiliary can attach to many verb stems: {走|はし}り{出|だ}す (start running), {泣|な}き{出|だ}す (burst into tears), {笑|わら}い{出|だ}す (start laughing). やり{出|だ}す is the most general form since やる covers doing anything.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {急|きゅう}にやり{出|だ}す: to suddenly start doing
- やり{出|だ}したら{止|と}まらない: once started, can't stop
- {勝手|かって}にやり{出|だ}す: to start doing on one's own

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {始|はじ}める: to begin — neutral and formal, works in all registers
- {取|と}りかかる: to set about; to get started on — emphasizes tackling a task
- し{出|だ}す: to start doing — similar compound but with する instead of やる, slightly more formal
